1339:
All alarm companies operating in Macon-Bibb County must be licensed and registered with the Tax Commissioner.
(Ord. No. O-14-0049, § 1, 9-2-2014; Ord. No. O-21-0081, § 1(Exh. A), 10-19-2021)
1340:
It shall be unlawful to key automatic dialer burglar alarms to the emergency number 911, or to Macon-Bibb County's switchboard. These types of alarms shall be keyed to a private service that can then notify the sheriffs department.
(Ord. No. O-14-0049, § 1, 9-2-2014)
1341:
(a) Underwriters' Laboratories (UL) approved equipment. All alarms shall be of Underwriters' Laboratories (UL) approved equipment and shall have complete electrical stand-by capacity.
(b) Circuits. All alarm circuits shall be installed in approved low voltage wire (PVC-coated).
(c) Connectors. All connectors used in the connection of all circuit wiring shall be either soldered or be an approved solderless connector.
(Ord. No. O-14-0049, § 1, 9-2-2014)
1342:
All alarm companies shall maintain an office with a telephone listing, and at least one (1) technician on twenty-four-hour call that can service alarms in the Macon-Bibb County area within sixty (60) minutes after activation.
(Ord. No. O-14-0049, § 1, 9-2-2014)
1343:
Upon any false burglar alarm being rendered, for any reason, by a burglar alarm system connected directly with the sheriff's department, or upon any false burglar alarm being communicated, for any reason, to the sheriff's department from any burglar alarm system not directly connected to the sheriff's department, the owner or operator of any such system is required, without notification, to submit a written report to the sheriff's department giving full details of the reasons behind the false alarm and the action taken to prevent future such occurrences. If the Food Truck is in possession of such permission form signed by the mayor, then such form shall be either on display or available to present immediately upon demand. The permission form required by this paragraph may be a form individually provided to one Food Truck, or may be in the form of a blanket permission granted to all Food Trucks operating as part of an authorized event or function.

1398:
The unlicensed practice of massage therapy has in certain contexts been associated with criminal behavior that damages the reputations of those who comply with the law as well as the communities in which these businesses operate. This is not a problem unique to Macon-Bibb County; it is an epidemic, occurring throughout the United States. As a result, a majority of the states, as well as the District of Columbia, have found it necessary to regulate message therapy and to provide for education and state certification. In these states, massage therapists must meet legal requirements to practice their profession, which may include minimum hours of training and passing an exam; Georgia is one of these states, requiring five hundred (500) educational hours including clinical work, an exam, and twenty-four (24) continuing education hours for each two-year license renewal period. [American Massage Therapy Association; O.C.G.A. § 43-24A-1 et seq.]
Businesses operating massage parlors with massage being offered by unlicensed masseuses and businesses of like character are businesses that affect the public health, safety, and general welfare of the communities in which they operate. Certain of these businesses have been associated with illegal sexual conduct, such as solicitation, pandering, pimping, prostitution, sodomy, lewdness, and other sexual conduct. In order to protect the public interest, health, and welfare, it is necessary that such businesses be regulated to prevent their use for unlawful and illegal activities. [FBI Weekly Reports 2009]
Therefore, based on the demonstrated experiences of the City of Macon, Georgia, Bibb County and other urban counties and municipalities, including but not limited to Atlanta, GA; Huntsville, AL; Kansas City, MO; Ashville, NC; Spartanburg County, SC; Seattle, WA; Phoenix, AZ; Champaign, IL; Pittsburgh, PA; Knoxville, TN; Augusta, ME, and Jacksonville, FL, which experiences are found to be relevant to the problems that face Macon-Bibb County, and based on the documentary evidence and oral testimony presented at public meetings by citizens, a number of whom are familiar with conditions in other localities, the Macon-Bibb County mayor and commission take note of the notorious and self-evident conditions and secondary effects attendant to the commercial exploitation of human sexuality, which do not vary greatly among the diverse communities within our country, especially the problems of crime, blight, and deterioration that are brought about by illegal sexual activities for hire.
Hence, Macon-Bibb County finds that it is in the best interest of health, welfare, safety, and morals; churches, schools, and parks; and the preservation of its businesses and neighborhoods to prevent the adverse impact of unlicensed massage practitioners and the parlors and businesses of like character wherein they practice illegal sexual activities for compensation. Therefore, Macon-Bibb County finds that the prohibition of unlicensed massage practice, as well as the prohibition of dispensation and consumption of alcohol and escort dating services in connection with, will improve the public welfare by furthering legitimate government interests, such as reducing criminal activity, protection against devaluation and deterioration of properties located nearby, and eliminating undesirable community conditions normally associated with parlors that have masseuses who are not licensed pursuant to the Georgia Massage Therapy Practice Act, and that such prohibition will not infringe upon the protected constitutional rights of freedom of speech. To that end, this section is hereby adopted.
(Ord. No. O-21-0081, § 1(Exh. A), 10-19-2021)

Act means the Georgia Massage Therapy Practice Act, enacted by and defined in O.C.G.A. § 43-24A-1 et seq., as amended.

For hire means a reasonable expectation that the person to whom the massage is provided, or some third person on his or her behalf, will pay money, give other consideration, or provide any gratuity therefore.

b. No license shall be issued to any massage parlor within Macon-Bibb County under this division unless every person who performs or offers to perform massage on its premises is a licensed massage therapist, and it shall be unlawful to operate as a massage parlor unless all such persons are and remain licensed massage therapists. (2) Macon-Bibb County license. No person shall operate a massage parlor without a valid, current, unrevoked, and unsuspended license from Macon-Bibb County, pursuant to this division.
(3) Conviction of a crime. No license under this section shall be issued or renewed to any person who shall have been convicted or shall have entered a plea of nolo contendere for any felony within ten (10) years, or two (2) misdemeanors within five (5) years, other than traffic violations, immediately prior to the filing of the application. Licenses granted to persons who fail to meet this requirement at any time shall be subject to revocation.
(4) Age of licensee; education. No person under the age of eighteen (18) shall be issued a license to operate a massage parlor. No license shall be issued to an applicant who does not have a high school diploma or its recognized equivalent.
(5) Personal residency; agent. (6) Corporate residency. All applications for licenses under this chapter by a corporation or other business entity shall name in the application one (1) or more residents in Macon-Bibb County as the agent and representative of the corporation to receive all communications, notices, services of process, or other papers or documents on behalf of the corporation in connection with any matter arising out of or connected with the issuance, holding, suspension, revocation, or other action with respect to any license issued pursuant to this division. The application shall give the mailing address of the person, and the mailing to any such person at such address of any notice required to be given under this chapter or any other law shall be sufficient notice to the corporation. If any such person shall cease to be a resident of Macon-Bibb County, another person shall immediately be appointed, in writing, in his place, and written notice shall be given to the Tax Commissioner, stating the name and address of the new agent.
(7) Annual license fee. The annual license fee shall be determined from time to time by the mayor and commission, based upon the reasonable costs of the actual regulatory activity, and listed in a schedule of fees and charges maintained by the Tax Commissioner.
(b) Application for license.
(1) To operate a massage parlor within Macon-Bibb County, the applicant must first make application to the Tax Commissioner on a form provided by the Tax Commissioner, or his designee, and that person, after having fully and truthfully completed such form and paying the prescribed fees and having received a license, shall maintain and operate such business pursuant to the ordinances of Macon-Bibb County and the laws of the state.
(2) Upon applying for a license with the Tax Commissioner, each applicant shall provide a true and correct copy or original of the state license for each and every massage practitioner, performing or anticipated to perform massage at its location, to the finance officer for inspection and copying. Failure of any massage practitioner to provide his or her state license shall automatically result in the denial of the issuance of a Macon-Bibb County license to the applicant.
(3) Subsequent to the Macon-Bibb County license being issued, the licensee shall, in person, furnish to the Tax Commissioner or his designee a true and correct copy or original of the state license of each new massage practitioner at the licensee's massage parlor prior to such person's commencing to perform or offering to perform massage at such massage parlor. When any massage practitioner discontinues performing massage at a massage parlor, the licensee shall make the departure known in writing to the Tax Commissioner within thirty (30) days of such departure.
(4) Each applicant for a license shall make his or her affidavit before the Tax Commissioner or his designee, on a form provided by the Tax Commissioner, upon oath, swearing or affirming that all persons practicing massage on the premises of his or her massage parlor are licensed massage therapists and that all requirements of this division for a license have been met.
(Ord. No. O-20-0070, § 6, 9-15-2020; Ord. No. O-21-0081, § 1(Exh. A), 10-19-2021)
1402:
Licenses for massage parlors shall expire on March 31st of each year and may be renewed on a calendar year basis, beginning January 1st of each year until March 31st of each year, provided that the licensee(s) continue to meet the requirements set out in this division and the requirements of the Act.
(Ord. No. O-21-0081, § 1(Exh. A), 10-19-2021)
1404:
(a) Each massage parlor shall post its license obtained pursuant to this division, along with the state license of each masseuse operating on the premises of such parlor, in a conspicuous place in the licensee's place of business and shall keep such licenses there at all times.
(b) Price rates for all services shall be prominently posted in the reception area or other conspicuous location available for all prospective customers. No service shall be allowed or permitted that is not prominently posted with its fees in such location.
1405: No massage parlor shall act as an escort or dating service.
1406: No alcoholic beverages shall be sold, served, given, dispensed, provided, consumed, or caused or allowed to be sold, served, given, dispensed, provided, consumed by or to any person on the premises of a massage parlor or kept thereon. Alcoholic beverages means and includes all types and kinds of alcohol as defined in the Alcoholic Beverages chapter of this Code of Ordinances.
1407:
(a) Massage parlors shall be open for business only between the hours of 6 a.m. and 11 p.m., inclusive.
(b) Any business holding a license issued under this division shall, at any time that the premises are open for business, be open to inspection by a law enforcement officer, the health department, license inspectors, and/or fire department inspectors.
1408: No person or business entity granted a location license pursuant to this division shall operate the business under a name not specified in the license nor conduct business at any location or place not specified in the license. No license shall be transferable. Upon the sale or relocation of a massage parlor, the license thereof shall be null and void.
1409: It shall be unlawful for any person or persons operating a massage parlor to permit persons under eighteen (18) years of age to enter the licensed premises unless such minor is accompanied by a parent or guardian, has the written, notarized permission of the parent or guardian, or has a written prescription from a physician, surgeon, osteopath, or podiatrist who has a valid current license, issued pursuant to Georgia law.
1410:
(a) Every portion of the premises of, and all equipment and supplies of, the massage parlor shall be kept clean and shall be operated in a sanitary condition.
(b) All employees and masseuses at each massage parlor shall wear clean, nontransparent outer garments, covering the breast, buttocks and genital areas.
1415:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any carnival, circus, tent show, or any other show of like nature, unless they shall first obtain a permit from the Tax Commissioner.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any street fair, carnival, or other tent shows to exhibit, or erect any tents, huts or houses for the purpose of exhibiting, on any of the streets, lanes or parks within Macon-Bibb County; provided, however, that nothing in this section shall be construed to make it unlawful to hold such exhibitions or shows, with the permission of the commission.
(c) Every circus, carnival company, traveling show, and every other person operating or showing in Macon-Bibb County, whether under auspices of any local organization or not, any so-called game of skill, the operation of which is legal under state laws, and for the playing of which any charge is made or accepted, shall pay to Macon-Bibb County a fee or tax in an amount to be determined from time to time by the commission and listed in the schedule of fees and charges maintained by the Tax Commissioner.
(Ord. No. O-21-0081, § 1(Exh. A), 10-19-2021)
1416:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to move, carry or otherwise transport houses, buildings, parts of buildings or other large structures through or across the streets of Macon-Bibb County without first having obtained a permit from the Tax Commissioner and approval of the sheriff's department.
(b) The Tax Commissioner is hereby delegated the duty and responsibility for issuing permits to applicants desiring to use the streets of Macon-Bibb County for moving houses, buildings, parts of buildings or other large objects.
(c) The permit required by this section shall constitute an additional requirement to any other requirements in this Code or state law.
(d) In determining whether a permit shall be issued, the Tax Commissioner and sheriff's department shall take into account the following factors in addition to any other factors as may be necessary to determine whether a proposed moving is in the public interest:
(1) The length of time required for the moving;
(2) The hours during which the moving is to take place and in particular whether the proposed moving conflicts with heavy traffic patterns;
(3) The route of the proposed moving; and
(4) The equipment and personnel available and employed for the proposed moving.
(e) If the Tax Commissioner or sheriff's department determines that the proposed moving of a structure hereunder would create a serious traffic hazard or otherwise be unreasonably dangerous to the public at large, either shall deny the application for a permit as required by this section. Otherwise the Tax Commissioner shall approve the application and issue the permit.
(Ord. No. O-21-0081, § 1(Exh. A), 10-19-2021)
